title: Packing Unit Cubes in a Cube of Side Just Below an Integer
content: Let \( s_{3}\left(n\right) \) be the side of the smallest cube that contains \( n \) non-overlapping unit cubes, rotations allowed. We prove that for every integer \( K \) ≥ 5, \( s_{3}\left(n\right)\lt K\quad \text{for\ all\ }n\leq K^{3}-15K^{3/2}-43K-10\sqrt{K}-12 \). To our knowledge no bound of the form \( s_{3}\left(n\right)\lt K \) was known beyond what stacking two-dimensional packings gives. By Nagamochi’s theorem \( s\left(K^{2}-2\right)=K \) for squares, a stacked (prism) packing in a cube of side less than \( K \) holds at most \( \left(K-1\right)\left(K^{2}-3\right) \) cubes; for every \( K≥301 \) our bound goes beyond every such packing. The proof is constructive: a core of axis-parallel cubes and three tilted bands placed along three walls, arranged cyclically so that each band is extruded only along an integer length and no layer is lost (the three-band rule). The same construction, together with a search on a structured \( {45}^{\circ } \) lattice, gives 60 new upper bounds for \( n \) < 1000, among them \( s_{3}\left(34\right)\lt 4 \), and explicit coordinates for Friedman’s 1998 bound \( s_{3}\left(33\right)\leq 3+\sqrt{2}/2 \). All packings are verified in exact arithmetic.
